claims.text: In situ high-resolution transmission electron microscopy equipped with a heating stage can reveal atomic-scale thermal behavior in nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The method can directly image temperature-induced structural changes and phase transitions.
The method can reveal elemental redistribution in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a uniform distribution of their constituent metals.
The nanoparticles will be heated incrementally from ambient to high temperatures under vacuum inside the TEM.
Atomic arrangements and grain-boundary configurations mediate phase changes.
Atomic arrangements and grain-boundary configurations mediate elemental segregation.
Thermal energy can overcome local bonding-energy barriers in the nanoparticles.
Overcoming local bonding-energy barriers triggers atomic reordering and phase transitions.
Heating may trigger elemental segregation driven by entropy effects.
Atomic reordering and phase-transition signatures will emerge at critical temperatures.
Changes in lattice fringes and diffraction patterns can serve as signatures of thermally induced structural changes.
At room temperature, the nanoparticles have no significant phase demarcations.
Thermal behavior observed under TEM vacuum may not represent behavior in reactive gas atmospheres.
Imaging alone may not capture all thermodynamic contributions to the observed behavior.
Attributing observed structural changes specifically to entropy-driven effects may require complementary spectroscopy or computational analysis.
